test_title: PYST 19: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: India adopted a policy of Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) after independence. Which of the following was a common limitation faced by ISI-led strategy by the 1980s?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Technological backwardness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• By the 1980s, India’s Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) strategy faced significant limitations such as **technological backwardness**, which hindered productivity and competitiveness.
 
• The focus on domestic production led to **limited access to advanced global technologies**, impacting innovation and modernization.
 
• Many industries under ISI were protected by high tariffs, creating a **lack of incentive to innovate or improve efficiency**.
 
• Technological stagnation resulted in **poor quality of goods** and inability to meet international standards, further limiting exports.
 
• Countries relying on ISI strategies often struggled with **low industrial diversification**, exacerbating technological deficiencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI):**

 
 
• ISI is an economic policy aimed at reducing dependency on imports by promoting domestic production of goods.
 
• It was widely adopted by developing countries post-World War II to foster industrial growth and economic independence.
 
 
 
• **Protectionism in ISI:**
 
 
• High import tariffs and quotas were imposed to protect domestic industries.
 
• While it encouraged initial industrial growth, it often led to inefficiency and lack of global competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Technological Stagnation:**
 
 
• Limited investment in research and development under ISI policies contributed to technological backwardness.
 
• Dependence on outdated technologies restricted productivity and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Shift to Liberalization:**
 
 
• India began liberalizing its economy in 1991, moving away from ISI towards globalization and free-market policies.
 
• This shift aimed to integrate India into the global economy and encourage technological advancements through foreign investments.
